data.title: Qantas to Retire All 10 Airbus A380s Starting in 2028, Four Years Earlier Than Planned
data.description: Qantas Group said it will gradually retire all 10 of its Airbus A380 aircraft starting in 2028, about four years earlier than previously planned, according to Jiemian News. The airline had originally planned to begin retiring the superjumbos in 2032 and replace them with more fuel-efficient Airbus and Boeing aircraft. Qantas said the decision was made because the delivery schedule for next-generation aircraft is "reassuring." It expects to save about A$300 million in net cash flow in fiscal years 2028 to 2031. The Airbus A380 entered service in 2007 and stopped production in 2021 after years of criticism over high fuel consumption, heavy maintenance costs and weak demand.

data.title: AI | Trustpilot CEO Says AI Search Demand Lifted Large Customers 35%
data.description:
Trustpilot Group Plc Chief Executive Officer Adrian Blair said demand from major brands seeking better visibility in artificial intelligence-powered searches helped drive a 35% increase in large customers on its platform in the first half, according to Bloomberg.

Blair made the comments as Trustpilot highlighted growing interest from brands in AI-powered search visibility.

data.title: Trump Administration Seeks Senate GOP Support for CLARITY Act
data.description:
The Trump administration is working to secure Senate Republican support for the CLARITY Act, while bank groups said Monday that recent revisions still do not make the stablecoin provisions acceptable. Some Republican senators, including John Cornyn of Texas, may side with banks and vote against the measure.

According to Foresight News, Cornyn said the latest text does not appear to address community banks' concerns about deposit outflows. The Council of Economic Advisers will launch an interactive tool on Tuesday that lets users set parameters and run scenarios to test its earlier conclusion that there is no significant link between stablecoin growth and community bank deposit outflows.

Patrick Witt, executive director of the President's Digital Asset Advisory Council, said the data show the banking lobby's deposit outflow narrative lacks support and that the bill includes safeguards for community banks. Democratic lawmakers also remain dissatisfied with the latest ethics language, saying it does not sufficiently restrict U.S. President Donald Trump and his family. Senator Adam Schiff said the provision does not effectively apply to the president and first family, while Mark Warner said the ethics language is far from adequate. Some Democrats are still negotiating changes before the vote.

data.title: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent Endorses Final CLARITY Act Draft
data.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent endorsed the final CLARITY Act draft on Monday, saying the legislation is essential to helping the U.S. win the global race for new technology. According to NS3.AI, Bessent said the draft would give the Treasury Secretary new authority to respond if stablecoins cause substantial deposit outflows from community banks. The bill still lacks bipartisan consensus and needs 60 votes to pass.

data.title: STOCKS | Shanghai Composite Falls For Fourth Day As China Data Misses Demand
data.description:
China's Shanghai Composite fell for a fourth straight session on Tuesday, closing down 0.54% at 3,864.28, while the Shenzhen Component lost 0.72% and the ChiNext Index dropped 1.15%, according to ETNet.

Turnover in Shanghai and Shenzhen totaled RMB 1.6 trillion, the lowest this year and down RMB 16.5 billion from the previous session. Consumer-related sectors led declines, with tourism down 5.3%, while the semiconductor supply chain rose 1.6%.

Separately, the yuan's onshore spot rate closed at 6.7134 per dollar, its weakest since September 3, while the central parity rate was set at 6.7670, up for a fifth straight session and the strongest since February 3, 2023. ETNet also reported that China's industrial output growth accelerated in August, but retail sales growth slowed and fixed-asset investment fell more than expected.

data.title: Oil Prices Rise While Gold and Silver Fall
data.description:
October New York crude rose $2.26, or 2.23%, to $103.65 at 5:00 PM, while November Brent crude gained $1.86, or 1.84%, to $102.85, according to ETNet.

London gold fell $22.87, or 0.53%, to $4,265.34, and New York gold futures dropped $56.30, or 1.28%, to $4,352.60. London silver declined $0.29, or 0.46%, to $62.84, while New York silver futures lost $1.32, or 2.02%, to $63.87.

data.title: India’s August Trade Deficit Narrows as Oil Risks Persist
data.description:
India’s trade deficit narrowed in August even as instability across the Middle East and little sign the US or Iran are ready to back down added to economic headwinds, according to Bloomberg.

The report did not provide the size of the deficit or additional trade figures.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | BofA Says Fear of Disorderly Bond Yield Rise Is Cooling Risk Appetite
data.description: Exuberance in risk assets is fading as investors worry about a chaotic rise in bond yields and the results of US midterm elections, according to a survey by Bank of America Corp., Bloomberg reported.

data.title: STOCKS | Khosla Says AI Era Calls for U.S. Tax Reform
data.description:
Conrad Masterson and Reginald Miller wrote that Vinod Khosla, founder of Khosla Ventures and co-founder of Sun Microsystems, said the AI era requires the United States to reform its tax code. According to Sina Finance, Khosla argued that AI will sharply reduce the labor needed to produce the same GDP, and said the tax system should shift from favoring capital to supporting workers.

He said AI could complete at least 80% of economically valuable work now done by humans, covering 80% of jobs, and estimated that underemployment or unemployment could reach 30% to 50%. Khosla also said the United States should consider ending capital gains tax preferences after the 2028 election, while keeping the budget balanced.

He proposed using new tax revenue to compensate workers affected by AI and to fund basic public services, including virtual primary care, specialized medical services, mental health support, chronic disease management, personalized tutoring, government services, and legal aid. Khosla also said the United States could consider an AI compute tax after 2030 if AI has a significant negative impact on jobs.

data.title: Moonrock Capital Founder Simon Dedic Says Senate Clarity Act Vote Is Expected in About 10 Hours
data.description:
Moonrock Capital founder Simon Dedic said on X that the Senate vote on the Clarity Act is expected in about 10 hours. According to Odaily, he said Democrats have verbally rejected the Republican draft over ethics concerns, while Polymarket odds have already collapsed and the market has priced in a failure.

Dedic said he is looking forward to the vote regardless of the outcome. He added that if the bill fails, the U.S. could receive equally strong crypto-supportive regulation from the SEC, and that Democrats would bear responsibility if the U.S. were to lose its leadership in frontier finance and see companies move offshore.

data.title: Thailand Considers 30% Levy on Imported EVs, Finance Minister Says
data.description: Thailand could impose an excise tax of about 30% on fully imported electric vehicles, Finance Minister Ekniti Nitithanprapas said, according to Bloomberg. He said the proposed levy is intended to steer automakers toward local production.

data.title: AI | Model ML Seeks Over $100 Million at More Than $1 Billion Valuation
data.description:
Model ML, which sells artificial intelligence software to investment banks and other financial institutions, is in talks to raise more than $100 million at a valuation above $1 billion, according to Bloomberg.

The startup’s software is aimed at reducing routine work for bankers.

data.title: STOCKS | Morgan Stanley Adds 15 Names to Its Europe Core Overweight List
data.description:
Morgan Stanley's strategy team made an unusually large overhaul of its high-conviction stock pool, recommending that investors broaden their exposure in European portfolios rather than focus only on market themes such as AI capital spending and defense. According to Sina Finance, the team led by Marina Zavolock said it favors a diversified allocation strategy rather than abandoning the AI investment theme.

Since the end of August, the team has added 15 overweight top picks, compared with the usual monthly addition of three to four names. The list now includes 43 overweight top picks, 60% of which were added over the past three months. The new additions span banks and financials, including ABN AMRO Bank, Lloyds Banking Group, Arden, and EQT; companies with their own stock-specific logic such as Accor, Shell, and Scout24; and firms benefiting from artificial intelligence and data center development, including Legrand, Kingspan, and Merlin Properties.

data.title: STOCKS | BofA Survey: Investors Still Bullish on Macro and AI Capex
data.description: A Bank of America survey showed investors still believe in improving macroeconomic conditions and rapid growth in artificial intelligence capital spending, but risks from a disorderly surge in bond yields and a Democratic landslide in the midterm elections have made market sentiment more cautious. According to Sina Finance, a strategist team led by Michael Hartnett wrote that the September Global Fund Manager Survey showed cash allocations rose from 3.5% to 3.9%, the biggest monthly increase since March, as excessive summer optimism faded. The report said risk exposure is appropriate only when cash allocations return to the neutral 4% to 5% range. Investors' net underweight in bonds reached 48%, the highest since May 2022, while the net overweight in stocks fell to 49% from 56% in the previous month.

data.title: Southern Philippines Regional Vote Points To No Majority
data.description: According to Nikkei Asia, initial results from the historic election for a regional assembly in the separatist-wracked southern Philippines indicate that no party is set to win a majority in the 80-seat parliament.

data.title: Marsh Lifts Treasury Weighting to Neutral as Yields Stay Elevated
data.description:
US investment consultancy Marsh is raising Treasury allocations in some portfolios it recommends to clients, according to Bloomberg.

The move reflects large investors’ efforts to take advantage of elevated yields.

data.title: AI | JPMorgan’s Sundar Says AI Trade Is in ‘Digestion’ Phase
data.description:
Sitara Sundar, head of alternative investment strategy at JPMorgan Private Bank, said the artificial intelligence trade is in a “digestion” phase and that the firm remains constructive on the AI industry over the long run, according to Bloomberg.

Speaking on Bloomberg Television, Sundar said JPMorgan would lean more into the integration and application layers of artificial intelligence.

data.title: Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi To Visit China On September 16
data.description:
China's Foreign Ministry said Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi will visit China on September 16, and Foreign Minister Wang Yi will hold talks with him, according to ETNet.

This will be Araghchi's second visit to China this year and comes ahead of the planned meeting between Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump. ETNet reported that Araghchi's previous visit in early May was his first trip to China since the U.S.-Iran conflict escalated, and that he briefed Wang on the latest status of U.S.-Iran talks and Iran's next steps.

data.title: AI TRENDS | Gates Foundation Plans at Least $1 Billion to Expand AI Access
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, the Gates Foundation plans to invest at least $1 billion over the next two years to improve access to artificial intelligence, and co-founder Bill Gates warned that the way AI is spread could widen the global wealth gap further. In a report, Gates wrote that if AI is properly guided, it will give more people solutions, opportunities, and knowledge that have long been out of reach, and that decisions over the next 12 to 18 months on how AI is built, funded, and deployed will determine whether the technology mainly benefits those with the most resources or reaches those with the least. The Gates Foundation plans to donate a cumulative $200 billion before it closes in 2045.

data.title: MediaTek Launches Dimensity 9600 Pro Flagship Chip on 2nm Process
data.description:
MediaTek unveiled its next-generation flagship chip, the Dimensity 9600 Pro, at its 2026 Dimensity flagship product launch on September 15. According to ChainCatcher, the chip uses TSMC's 2nm process and contains more than 33 billion transistors.

The company said the chip adopts a fused computing architecture that integrates CPU, GPU, NPU, and ISP cores around AI. It features an all-big-core design with two C2-Ultra cores at 4.55GHz, three C2-Pro cores at 4.35GHz, and three C2-Pro cores at 3.1GHz, along with 34.5MB of L2+L3+ system cache. It also supports LPDDR6 memory and UFS 5.0 storage.

MediaTek said the Dimensity 9600 Pro's big-core power consumption is down 37% and multi-core power consumption is down 61% versus the Dimensity 9500. In GeekBench V6.4, it scored 4,276 in single-core and 12,650 in multi-core tests, up about 17% and 15%, respectively, from the Dimensity 9500. The NPU uses a dual-NPU architecture with the APU 1090, and peak performance is said to be up 51%. MediaTek also said it has ranked first in global smartphone SoC market share for six consecutive years.
